segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Some Pharisees came to him to test him, asking,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is it permitted for a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why then did Moses command us to give a certificate of dismissal and divorce her?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It was because of your hardness of heart that Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been this way.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I tell you, whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “If that is how it is for a man with his wife, it is better not to marry.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by people, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens. Let the one who is able to accept this accept it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then children were brought to him so that he might lay his hands on them and pray, but the disciples rebuked them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Leave the children alone, and do not stop them from coming to me, for the kingdom of the heavens belongs to such as these.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And after laying his hands on them, he went on from there.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then someone came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why do you ask me about what is good? There is only one who is good. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Which ones?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “‘You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not give false testimony.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Honor your father and mother,’ and ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The young man said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I have observed all these. What do I still lack?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you want to be complete, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens. Then come, follow me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the young man heard this, he went away grieving, for he had much property.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, it will be hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of the heavens.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who then can be saved?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked straight at them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “For human beings this is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Peter responded,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, we have left everything and followed you. What then will there be for us?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

notes.note: Older versions have “tempting him.” The Greek verb means to put someone to the test, here by a question meant to trap, and modern English “tempt” has narrowed to enticing someone to sin. Most recent translations also use “test” in this verse.

The question reflects a live dispute over Deuteronomy 24:1, which allows a man to divorce his wife if he finds “something indecent” in her. According to later rabbinic tradition, the school of Shammai limited this to sexual misconduct, while the school of Hillel allowed divorce for almost any fault. The Pharisees are pressing Jesus to take a side.

The Greek word is a broad term for unlawful sexual activity. Most interpreters take it here to mean a wife’s sexual unfaithfulness; others limit it to unchastity before marriage, or to marriages within the forbidden degrees of kinship in Leviticus 18. The exception appears only in Matthew (here and 5:32), and its scope is disputed.

notes.phrase: and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery
notes.note: Many early manuscripts lack this final clause, and several critical editions and modern translations omit it as a possible carry-over from 5:32. The SBLGNT text translated here includes it.

“This saying” may point back to Jesus’ teaching on marriage and divorce (verses 4–9) or to the disciples’ remark that it is better not to marry. The second fits the words about eunuchs that follow and is the more common view, but both are defended.

Matthew’s Greek has the plural, “the heavens,” a Semitic turn of phrase that a first-century hearer would have noticed. Most translations flatten it to “the kingdom of heaven.” The phrase means the same as “the kingdom of God,” which Matthew uses in verse 24.

Eunuchs—castrated men, often court officials—were a familiar figure in the ancient world, and the Law of Moses excluded them from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:1). The third group is almost universally understood as a figure of speech for those who give up marriage for the sake of the kingdom, not as literal self-mutilation.

notes.phrase: Why do you ask me about what is good? There is only one who is good.
notes.traditional: Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God
notes.note: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, that is, God,” matching Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19. The earlier manuscripts have the wording translated here, and the other reading is generally regarded as a harmonization to the parallel accounts.

The traditional rendering is “perfect.” The Greek word describes what has reached its goal or lacks nothing—whole, complete, mature—and in the Greek Old Testament it is used of people wholly devoted to God. “Complete” also answers the young man’s question, “What do I still lack?” “Perfect” remains the standard rendering and is defensible, but in modern English it suggests flawlessness.

The image is a deliberate exaggeration: the largest animal of the region and the smallest familiar opening. The popular explanation that “the Needle’s Eye” was a small gate in Jerusalem has no ancient evidence behind it. The disciples’ reaction in verse 25 shows they understood the saying to mean “impossible.”

notes.phrase: at the renewal of all things
notes.note: The Greek is a single word meaning “rebirth” or “renewal,” used in the period for the restoration of the world or of a nation after catastrophe. Here it refers to the renewed world of the age to come. Older versions have “in the regeneration”; many modern versions have “the renewal of all things” or “the new world.”
Some important early manuscripts lack “or wife,” and a few read “many times as much” instead of “a hundred times as much.” Critical editions differ on both points; the SBLGNT text is translated here.

candidates.reason: Recurs across the Gospels, Acts, Paul and Revelation, and versions vary between “fornication,” “unchastity,” “sexual immorality” and “prostitution,” which affects how the divorce exception and the apostolic decree are read.
Recurs in Matthew 5:48, Paul, Hebrews and James, where translators split between “perfect,” “mature” and “complete,” and readers would be misled by unexplained variation.
The same verb means “divorce,” “send away,” “release” and “dismiss” in different contexts, and the divorce passages in Matthew, Mark and Luke need one consistent rendering.
Extremely frequent across the New Testament, and translators variously use “behold,” “look,” “see,” “suddenly” or omit it, so a policy for its narrative and speech uses is needed.
Covers physical healing, rescue from danger and final salvation across all books, and a rule is needed for when “save,” “heal” or “rescue” is used.
